text:
neha: FYI - autotuner sweep on p4d surfaced a tail-regression when FlashAttention is selected for causal attention on non-32-aligned head_dim (48 / 56). dropping profiler snippets and a suggested short-term mitigation.

sam: paste profiler lines? :eyes:

neha: condensed: 
```
seq=512  hd=48  causal=true  -> flashattn_v2 chosen   -> p50=6.4ms  p95=14.2ms
seq=512  hd=48  causal=true  -> sdpa_fallback chosen -> p50=4.1ms  p95=6.8ms
seq=256  hd=56  causal=true  -> flashattn_v2 chosen   -> p50=3.2ms  p95=7.9ms
seq=2048 hd=64  causal=true  -> flashattn_v3 chosen   -> p50=18.2ms p95=35.9ms
```
Autotuner rule today: prefer flash_attn_v2 when head_dim < 64 && seq <= 768. Some hd values show worse tails.

yuki: are we recording kernel_name + batch runtimes in traces? need to correlate.

neha: yep - we log selected_kernel, measured samples, feature vector. sampling window is 1h for rule recompute.

jordan: my read: v2's causal path triggers extra permute/memcpy for head_dim % 32 != 0 -> misaligned loads -> thread divergence -> p95 cliffs. packing layout and small launch variance can flip cost.

sam: reproduced locally on A100 sm80 - observed an extra memcpy path in a v2 build when hd%32 != 0.

infra-bot: autotuner: run 2025-02-07T08:11:02 id=rt-10021

marta: proposed short-term: special-case prefer SDPA for head_dim in {48,56} when seq in [256,1024] && causal=true. canary looked good.

neha: i ran a 5% canary with that rule. before/after (same model traffic):
baseline (autotuner): seq=512 hd=48 causal p95=14.2ms
special-case SDPA:        seq=512 hd=48 causal p95=6.9ms
-> throughput increased ~28% on affected slices, tails much improved.

sam: rather than hardcode dims, suggest heuristic: if head_dim % 32 != 0 && head_dim < 96 then bias to SDPA for seq <= 1024. catches 48/56 and doesn't touch 96/128.

yuki: also note causal vs non-causal kernels diverge: flashattn_v3 has a faster non-causal path; causal may still be v2-like in some compile configs. include that in decision vector.

jordan: we should expand autotuner features: add kernel build tags and compile-time flags (sm_target, fp_mode, flashattn_causal_opt). ticket RUNTIME-1482 opened.

neha: short-term plan: push heuristic hotfix (rollbackable). medium-term: expand tuner dims & retrain; long-term: headroom-aware objective (not just median throughput).

marta: rollout: gate 5% canary for 24h + regression alert if p95 increases >10% vs baseline.

neha: adding extra trace fields: selected_kernel, fallback_reason, measured_p50, measured_p95, sample_count, kernel_build_tag. also will log kernel_fallback_reason whenever SDPA chosen over FlashAttn.

sam: add kernel build tag (e.g. flashattn_v2_causal_opt=true) to traces so we can tie regressions to binary variants. also include memcpy/permute counters if available.

neha: local repro command I used:
```
./tools/run_attention_bench.sh --seq 512 --batch 8 --heads 16 --head-dim 48 --causal true --iters 200
```

yuki: can we add a CI micro-benchmark that sweeps head_dim mod 32 to detect alignment cliffs early?

jordan: i'll add a tiny wrapper to record memcpy counts and shared mem usage per kernel to help debug alignment-induced shuffles.

sam: after staging canary, run 99th-percentile headroom test on dedicated GPUs to validate tails under sustained load.

neha: PR for hotfix going up today. tagging @eng-sre for rollout checks. staging deploy queued (canary=5%).

infra-bot: deploy queued: patch/RUNTIME-1482-hotfix -> staging (canary=5%)

neha: will post staged perf and canary report in this thread after 12h. plan summary: short-term heuristic + richer logging; medium-term tuner expansion; long-term retrain with tail-aware objective.

marta: thanks. if safe we keep heuristic until tuner learns edge cases.

neha: also adding follow-ups to RUNTIME-1482: CI head_dim sweep, export memcpy metrics, and timeline for retrain.

sam: small ask: please ensure decision logs include selected_kernel, fallback_reason, measured_p50, measured_p95, and sample_count for postmortem.

neha: adding those fields now. will attach trace ids in follow-up. :thumbsup:
